identity: Mono-black discard-and-attrition control, and the deck is labelled honestly rather than aspirationally. The brief called this archetype 'Draw-Denial Stax'; the Phase 9 grill established that Mornsong Aria does not deny draws in any meaningful sense - 'searches their library for a card, puts it into their hand' REPLACES a random draw with an unrestricted tutor at unchanged rate, so it is card-quality POSITIVE for the opponent, and its only true denial is against the cube's bulk-draw text (29 of 282 pool cards) and its lifegain (13 of 277). What the deck actually does: 5 copies of hand attack plus 5 removal spells trade one-for-one against a resource base the opponent refills at exactly one card per turn while Aria is out, 5 refuel copies that all function under the lock, and a 6-copy evasive clock closes. Two limits are stated rather than hidden. First, all 5 hand-attack copies are SORCERY-speed while Aria hands the opponent its tutored card at their own draw step - so the tutored card is reachable only after they have had a full main phase to use it, and only 3 of the 5 copies let the pilot choose what is taken. Second, Aria is a rare capped at one copy with no enchantment tutor in the pool, so under the assembly gate's own model it is seen 33% of the time by turn 9; the deck is therefore built to win WITHOUT it and Aria is recorded as an accelerant, not an engine.

card_pool_rules.extra_constraint: max 5 rare+mythic total across mainboard and sideboard

checklist.base: cube_mainboard - every card verified present in the working pool by exact name.
checklist.copy_limits: Commons and uncommons capped at 2, rares and mythics at 1; the Phase 5C validator cross-checked every combined mainboard+sideboard count against cube_search.get_max_copies and returned PASS.
checklist.rare_mythic_budget: 5 of the maximum 5, fully spent: Mornsong Aria (rare, MB), Shadow Urchin (rare, MB), Deceit (mythic, MB), Emptiness (mythic, MB), Dawnhand Dissident (rare, SB). The Phase 9 repair swapped Taster of Wares (rare) for Emptiness (mythic), keeping the total unchanged.
checklist.basics: 18 Swamp - format-supplied and exempt from copy limits.
checklist.colour: All 19 distinct nonland cards return a usable 'cast' mode from effective_cost.best_mode against core_colors ['B']; the five hybrid cards (Shadow Urchin {2}{B/R}, Deceit {4}{U/B}{U/B} with Evoke {U/B}{U/B}, Emptiness {4}{W/B}{W/B} with Evoke {W/B}{W/B}, Reaping Willow {1}{W/B}{W/B}{W/B}, Mischievous Sneakling {1}{U/B}) are cast entirely off Swamps, so splash_colors is empty. Both Incarnations' 'if {B}{B} was spent to cast it' clauses are satisfied by paying their hybrid pips with black mana.

At the beginning of each player's draw step, that player loses 3 life, searches their library for a card, puts it into their hand, then shuffles.

sideboard.name: Dawnhand Dissident
sideboard.oracle_text:
{T}, Blight 1: Surveil 1.
{T}, Blight 2: Exile target card from a graveyard.
During your turn, you may cast creature spells from among cards you own exiled with this creature by removing three counters from among creatures you control in addition to paying their other costs.
sideboard.when_to_board: Vs the cube's 39 graveyard-interaction cards. '{T}, Blight 2: Exile target card from a graveyard' is repeatable only while other bodies exist to absorb counters - Dissident is a 1/2 and two counters kill it - so realistic throughput is one exile per turn at the cost of shrinking your own board. '{T}, Blight 1: Surveil 1' at half the cost is the mode you will use more often.

sideboard.name: Rooftop Percher
sideboard.oracle_text:
Changeling (This card is every creature type.)
Flying
When this creature enters, exile up to two target cards from graveyards. You gain 3 life.
sideboard.when_to_board: Vs reanimator and flashback decks; 'exile up to two target cards from graveyards' on a 3/3 flier that also joins the clock. The 'gain 3 life' rider is dead whenever your own Aria is out.

sideboard.name: Darkness Descends
sideboard.oracle_text: Put two -1/-1 counters on each creature.
sideboard.when_to_board: Vs token and go-wide decks ONLY. 'Put two -1/-1 counters on each creature' is the only mass creature effect in the pool castable off Swamps, but it is not one-sided: of this deck's 7 distinct creature names it kills Bile-Vial Boggart, Heirloom Auntie and Dream Seizer outright, leaving Shadow Urchin (3/4 to 1/2), Dawnhand Eulogist (3/3 to 1/1) and a hard-cast Deceit (5/5 to 3/3). Hold your own creatures in hand and cast them after it resolves.

sideboard.name: Blight Rot
sideboard.oracle_text: Put four -1/-1 counters on target creature.
sideboard.when_to_board: Vs 4-toughness threats. 'Put four -1/-1 counters on target creature' at instant speed outranges everything in the maindeck: Nameless Inversion caps at -3 toughness and evoked Emptiness at three counters. Run the full 2 copies - a 1-of is only found 33% of the time by turn 9.

sideboard.name: Reaping Willow
sideboard.oracle_text:
Lifelink
This creature enters with two -1/-1 counters on it.
{1}{W/B}, Remove two counters from this creature: Return target creature card with mana value 3 or less from your graveyard to the battlefield. Activate only as a sorcery.
sideboard.when_to_board: Vs aggro, which is this deck's worst matchup. {1}{W/B}{W/B}{W/B} is cast as {1}{B}{B}{B} off Swamps; a 3/6 body walls almost every ground attacker in the cube, and '{1}{W/B}, Remove two counters from this creature: Return target creature card with mana value 3 or less from your graveyard to the battlefield' rebuys Bile-Vial Boggart, Heirloom Auntie or Shadow Urchin. Its lifelink is dead under Aria; the toughness is what you are buying.

sideboard.name: Mischievous Sneakling
sideboard.oracle_text:
Changeling (This card is every creature type.)
Flash
sideboard.when_to_board: Vs faster aggro; Flash lets a 2/2 ambush an attacker without spending a sorcery-speed turn. A vanilla body - it is here for the instant-speed blocking, nothing else.

strategy_es: Ruta 2 — Desgaste con bloqueo de mano (Stax de negación de robo)
identity_es: Control mono negro de descarte y desgaste, y el mazo está etiquetado con honestidad y no con aspiración. El encargo llamó a este arquetipo 'Draw-Denial Stax'; se estableció que Mornsong Aria no niega robos en ningún sentido significativo: 'searches their library for a card, puts it into their hand' SUSTITUYE un robo aleatorio por un tutor sin restricciones al mismo ritmo, así que es POSITIVA en calidad de cartas para el rival, y su única negación real es contra el texto de robo masivo del cubo (29 de 282 cartas del pool) y su ganancia de vida (13 de 277). Lo que el mazo hace de verdad: 5 copias de ataque a la mano más 5 hechizos de eliminación intercambian uno a uno contra una base de recursos que el rival rellena a exactamente una carta por turno mientras Aria está fuera, 5 copias de reabastecimiento que funcionan todas bajo el bloqueo, y un reloj evasivo de 6 copias cierra. Dos límites se enuncian en vez de esconderse. Primero, las 5 copias de ataque a la mano son a velocidad de CONJURO mientras Aria entrega al rival su carta buscada en su propio paso de robar, así que la carta buscada solo es alcanzable después de que hayan tenido una fase principal completa para usarla, y solo 3 de las 5 copias dejan elegir al piloto qué se llevan. Segundo, Aria es una rara limitada a una copia sin tutor de encantamientos en el pool, así que bajo el propio modelo de la puerta de ensamblaje se ve el 33% de las veces para el turno 9; el mazo está construido por tanto para ganar SIN ella y Aria queda registrada como acelerante, no como motor.
